title: the Node global scope and the CommonJS module wrapper are host facilities, and four of them do not exist in the emitted ESM at all
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Host Globals'. This case is also the backend-agreement pin for the ambient name environment: the reference frontend runs against the installed @types packages and the pinned fork carries none, so before the rule was inverted `Buffer`/`require`/`module` were clean here and TS2591 there, and `global`/`exports`/`__dirname`/`__filename`/`setImmediate` were clean here and TS2304 there. A corpus case cannot see that divergence unless the language itself answers, which is why these names are refused BY NAME rather than left to whichever ambient lib is installed. `__dirname`, `__filename`, `module`, and `exports` are worse than unportable: the compiler emits ESM, where they are a guaranteed ReferenceError inside a function whose row reads `failures: []`.
